item.title: Custody of one child does not dilute husband's duty to maintain wife and other child living with her: Delhi High Court
item.description: Delhi High Court held that custody of one child does not dilute husband's maintenance obligation under Section 125 CrPC to maintain wife and other child living with her.

item.title: Cyril Amarchand Mangaldas advised SkyPower Group
item.description: Cyril Amarchand Mangaldas advised SkyPower Group on the acquisition of SkyPower Southeast Solar India Private Limited by Inox Neo Energies Limited, involving a 50 MW solar photovoltaic power project in Madhya Pradesh.

item.title: Karta's liability for HUF debts is personal and unlimited; 'Seat Court' retains jurisdiction to enforce award beyond territorial limits: Bombay HC
item.description: Bombay High Court observes that in case of HUF debts, liability of Karta is personal and unlimited, and Seat Court retains jurisdiction to enforce award beyond territorial limits.

item.title: S. 3 Judges (Inquiry) Act 1st proviso doesn't negate individual authority of Parliament; Art. 32 remedy confined only to fundamental rights enforcement: SC
item.description: Supreme Court has held that 1st proviso of S. 3 Judges (Inquiry) Act doesn't negate individual authority of Parliament to initiate impeachment proceeding against High Court Judge

item.title: Employee entitled to TDS credit despite non- deposit of deducted tax by the employer: Gujarat High Court
item.description: TDS not deposited by employer? Explore Gujarat High Court ruling on employees' right to claim TDS credit

item.title: UGC Issues Guidelines for Mental Health and Well-Being in Higher Educational Institutions
item.description: UGC guidelines for mental health in HEIs outlines key objectives, required centres, helplines, staffing ratios, and compliance steps for campuses.

item.description: Delhi High Court extends the ad hoc licensing arrangement in the PPL Pass Code Hospitality copyright dispute pending Supreme Court decision on licensing authority.

item.description: Analysis of Section 173(3) BNSS on FIR registration, police discretion and statutory interpretation under India’s new criminal law.
